prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a high-quality costume-and-anatomy concept sheet for ONE original Western high-fantasy wizard, focused on hands, wrists and robe sleeves, for later 3D modeling. NOT a UI screen, not a selection grid of several outfits.
The previous attempts were explicitly REJECTED: small hands and thin wrists attached to substantial sleeves, and ordinary workwear with tiny stars. Correct BOTH problems. Do not recreate those previous outfits.
Input roles:
Image 1 is a real orthographic measurement render of the existing human mesh. Left is the old sleeve around the hand, right is the same source bare arm, at the same scale. Use the right-hand bare-arm column only to understand continuous elbow/forearm/wrist/hand anatomy. It is a diagnostic, not the desired new silhouette. In particular make the new wrists perceptibly fuller and the hands substantial relative to the dressed arms; do not copy the old narrow wrist.
Image 2 is approved room atmosphere and softly stylized 3D material language. Keep the warm wood, amber hearth and cool night mood.
Image 3 is Gandalf clothing reference: use authentic robe sleeve structure, a restrained bell opening and a falling lower sleeve edge behind the wrist. Do not copy his identity, hat, staff, face or entire costume.
Image 4 is Dumbledore clothing reference: use supple formal robe fabric, layered sleeve construction and a broad integrated embroidered facing, not modern shirts or workwear cuffs. Do not copy his identity or exact designs.
Target: 1536 x 1024 landscape concept sheet with exactly TWO complementary views of the SAME outfit, not two alternatives. No text, no labels, no infographic, no ruler or numerical claims. Left two-thirds is the hero modeling view: one clothed right arm from just above elbow down to the entire hand and all fingertips, gently diagonal, dorsal three-quarter view with minimal foreshortening, elbow and wrist clearly readable. It enters naturally from the upper-left edge, hand near center-bottom, relaxed extended fingers, all five digits visible, not holding anything. Thin clean gutter. Right one-third is a smaller contextual view of the SAME two sleeves and large adult hands resting at a large open green leather book in the approved private study. It is a static wardrobe inspection pose, not an animation redesign. Do not reproduce the old near-camera huge sleeve/small distant hand perspective.
Anatomy priority: robust but elegant adult human hands and wrists, neither childish nor skeletal, each hand exactly five digits with plausible thumb, knuckle and finger-length relationships. Natural short nails and skin. Full wrist-to-middle-fingertip length should read approximately three-quarters of the true elbow-to-wrist forearm length in the neutral view, using the same depth and scale. Design size guide only: approximately 19.5 cm complete hand, around 26-28 cm actual forearm, palm across metacarpals about 9 cm, wrist about 6 cm wide, smoothly widening proximally. These are visual design targets, not printed specifications or proof of anatomical accuracy. Preserve substantial forearm thickness; the user ACCEPTS the previous forearm fullness. Do not solve this by shrinking arms, narrowing palms, elongating thin fingers or making huge puffy sleeves. Sleeve opening must not swallow the wrist; show a short, clear skin transition from a full wrist into palm.
Costume must immediately read as WESTERN FANTASY WIZARD through flowing robe construction, layered sleeve opening, rich cloth and confident arcane ornament integrated with tailoring. Moderate fitted forearm body with a visible under-sleeve plus a shaped, softly flared outer robe hem dropping BELOW the wrist and BEHIND the hand, clear of fingers. No rigid gauntlet shape. No work shirt, chore jacket, denim, canvas, sackcloth, hiking leather straps, small button tabs, rib-knit cuffs, uniform, armor, or simple straight sleeve with one little star. No staff or magic effects used to disguise weak clothing design.
Style: polished gentle stylized 3D fantasy concept, believable anatomy, tactile cloth with simplified clear forms matching the room; no hyperreal pores or extreme veins. Warm neutral skin shared between views, comfortable middle-weight physique; no face, no age or gender emphasis. Dark warm grey understated backdrop in hero view, readable amber/cool fill, physically legible fabric. Keep both hands large enough to judge in the context view. One original costume only.
Direction name: Amethyst Arcanist.
Original Western high-fantasy scholar-mage robe in deep aubergine and muted royal violet, with burgundy-purple silk lining and a fitted dark-violet inner sleeve. Soft silk-wool brocade with broad calm folds, luxurious but lived-in. The outer sleeve has a clear short bell shape with a softly pointed underside that drapes backward from the wrist; it is fabric, not a rigid vambrace. A broad antique-gold embroidered facing, around 3-4 cm in apparent cloth width, follows the shaped opening and carries an original connected arcane geometric sigil pattern, worked into the weave. The facing should look part of a robe's continuous decorative vocabulary, not a badge stuck on a jacket. A faint larger-scale damask pattern in the violet sleeve body. Show inner sleeve, lining, embroidered facing, full natural wrist and mature adult hand as four distinct coherent layers. No white shirt cuffs, no buttons, no leather, no fingerless gloves, no glowing runes. The human hand and wrist must have enough width and volume to visually balance the accepted medium-full arm. The wardrobe should plausibly belong to the master of the magical hearth study, with unmistakable mage identity.
